references.text: Herod hears about Jesus and is confused about who he is. [ref:Luk 9:7-9|Luke 9:7-9] shows Herod Antipas' earlier interest in Jesus, which forms the background for the threat to kill him in Luke 13:31.
Jesus had already turned his face toward Jerusalem ([ref:Luk 9:51-53|Luke 9:51-53]). His journey to Jerusalem could not be stopped by Herod's threats, for he was following God's plan.
Herod Antipas finally meets Jesus face to face during the trial ([ref:Luk 23:6-12|Luke 23:6-12]). This is the fulfillment of the confrontation that the Pharisees warned about in 13:31.

Even as a child, Jesus was threatened by a Herod (Herod the Great) who wanted to kill him ([ref:Matt 2:13-16|Matthew 2:13-16]). Here it is Herod Antipas, the son, who threatens Jesus' life – a parallel showing that the Herodian dynasty repeatedly stood against God's Messiah.

Jesus' answer in [ref:Luk 13:32-33|Luke 13:32-33] is the immediate continuation, where he calls Herod a "fox" and declares that he must continue on his way, for a prophet cannot die outside Jerusalem.

Herod Antipas' character and his killing of John the Baptist ([ref:Mark 6:14-20|Mark 6:14-20]) provide background for why the Pharisees consider the threat real – Herod had already shown willingness to kill a prophet.

Jesus deliberately avoided Judea because the Jews there sought to kill him ([ref:Joh 7:1|John 7:1]). Similar death threats met Jesus from various sides, and he acted according to God's timing rather than human threats.
Plans to kill Jesus were widespread among the authorities ([ref:Joh 11:53-54|John 11:53-54]). Herod's threat is part of the broader picture of opposition against Jesus.

In the early church's prayer, Herod (Antipas) is mentioned together with Pontius Pilate as those who stood united against Jesus ([ref:Apg 4:27-28|Acts 4:27-28]), confirming that Herod's hostility toward Jesus was real, but that everything happened according to God's counsel and will.

The Pharisees had an ambiguous relationship with Jesus. In [ref:Luk 12:1|Luke 12:1] Jesus warns against the hypocrisy of the Pharisees, which makes their motives for warning him in 13:31 ambiguous – they may have wanted to scare him away from the area.
